text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning. - - -

French President Jacques Chirac proposed a biannual summit be held as of 1998 between leaders of the European Union and Mercosur countries. Chirac is visiting Brazil in the first step of a four country Latin American tour.
The Lower House approved by an overwhelming majority a new bill which will put an end to the Brazilian state's 40 year monopoly over the oil sector and open it up to private investment.
-- PEUGEOT MAY BENEFIT FROM BRAZIL QUOTA SYSTEM

Brazil agreed to extend fiscal benefits to French automaker Peugeot if it decides to open up a manufacturing plant in the country in exchange for France's support for the Cardoso administration's controversial automotive regime which has already generated a flood of protests at the World Trade Organization.
-- BANKER LINKS SAO PAULO MAYOR TO BOND SCANDAL

Sao Paulo mayor Celso Pitta was linked to a growing illegal bond scandal when a banker, who is accused of profiting from the bond scheme, accused Pitta of having been involved in preliminary talks for a major bond issue in the state of Pernambuco.
-- ARGENTINA IS PRIORITY SAYS CARDOSO TO CHIRAC

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso told French President Jacques Chirac that the commercial relationship with Argentina was Brazil's top bilateral priority. He compared the Brazilian-Argentine relationship to that of France and Germany in the 1950's at the start of the European Economic Communtiy.
-- CHIRAC AGREES TO DISCUSS TRADE BARRIERS
In talks with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso French President Jacques Chirac agreed to discuss European Union agricultural trade barriers.
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
